_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from Shiori's documentation; no upstream egg.
name: Shiori
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Shiori is a simple bookmark manager that keeps a readable copy of every page you save. The egg runs it with SQLite and gives the owner account the username and password you set, instead of Shiori's well-known default login.
startup: export SHIORI_DIR=/home/container/data SHIORI_HTTP_SECRET_KEY="$(cat data/.secret-key)"; if [ ! -f data/.raptor-owner ]; then [ -n "{{OWNER_PASSWORD}}" ] || { echo "Set Owner password first: until it is set, anyone could sign in to Shiori's default account."; exit 1; }; ./shiori server -a 127.0.0.1 -p {{SERVER_PORT}} --access-log=false >/dev/null 2>&1 & p=$!; t=; for i in $(seq 60); do sleep 1; r=$(curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"shiori","password":"gopher"}' http://127.0.0.1:{{SERVER_PORT}}/api/v1/auth/login) && { t=$(echo "$r" | jq -r '.message.token // empty'); break; }; done; if [ -n "$t" ]; then jq -n --arg u "{{OWNER_USERNAME}}" --arg p "{{OWNER_PASSWORD}}" '{username: $u, old_password: "gopher", new_password: $p}' | curl -sf -o /dev/null -X PATCH -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $t" --data-binary @- http://127.0.0.1:{{SERVER_PORT}}/api/v1/auth/account || { kill $p; echo "Shiori didn't accept the owner account's new name or password."; exit 1; }; echo "Set up the owner account {{OWNER_USERNAME}}."; fi; kill $p; wait $p; touch data/.raptor-owner; fi; exec ./shiori server -p {{SERVER_PORT}}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Shiori: downloads Shiori from its GitHub releases, checked against
# GitHub's SHA-256, and makes the key that signs logins. The bookmarks
# (the data folder) are never touched, and the binary is only replaced
# once the new one is complete.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=x86_64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=aarch64 ;;
    *) fail "Shiori has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
tag=$(gh-release tag go-shiori/shiori "$version") || exit 1

if [ -x shiori ] && [ "$(cat .shiori-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Shiori $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Shiori $tag"
    gh-release download go-shiori/shiori "$tag" "shiori_Linux_${arch}_${tag#v}.tar.gz" "$work/shiori.tar.gz"
    tar -xzf "$work/shiori.tar.gz" -C "$work" shiori
    install -m 0755 "$work/shiori" shiori.new
    mv -f shiori.new shiori
    echo "$tag" > .shiori-version
fi

mkdir -p data
# The key that signs logins, made once: a new one would sign everyone out.
if [ ! -s data/.secret-key ]; then
    (umask 077; openssl rand -hex 32 > data/.secret-key)
fi
echo "Installed Shiori $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Shiori version to install, such as 1.8.0, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Owner username
variables.description: The owner account's username, set on the first start. Change it in Shiori's settings afterwards.

variables.name: Owner password
variables.description: The owner account's password, set on the first start. Change it in Shiori's settings afterwards.
